review_notes: The principal question is whether restatements increase the pricing of discretionary information risk. Section 3.3 explicitly gives two approaches to that question: firm-specific event-time Eq. (1)/Table 2 and monthly cross-sectional Eq. (2)/Table 3; retain both as the paper’s paired H1 tests. The CAR association in Eq. (3)/Table 5, restatement-characteristic interactions in Eq. (4)/Table 6, the non-restatement industry-peer test, and the cost-of-capital arithmetic are later applications or follow-up questions, not part of the selected principal family.

The two retained factor-loading models require AQ factor construction. Eq. (5) generates residuals used to form AQ; Eq. (6) partitions AQ into DiscAQ residuals and InnateAQ fitted values. The supplied verified mathematical tails resolve the Eq. (1) event-month boundary, Eq. (5) lag, and fiscal-year t+1 portfolio timing. Eq. (5) and Eq. (6) estimator names are not stated; the exact TCA item calculation and Eq. (6) log bases are also not reported.
results_review_notes: Only the two frozen H1 baseline specifications are reported: the firm-specific event-time Eq. (1)/Table 2 model and the monthly cross-sectional Eq. (2)/Table 3 model. Later CAR, duration, restatement-characteristic, and cost-of-capital tests are excluded.

Table 2 reports mean firm-level OLS coefficients from 299 firm regressions, each estimated over 73 monthly event-time observations. Table 3 reports pre/post means and differences across 36 and 37 monthly cross-sectional coefficient estimates, respectively; each monthly cross-section uses the 299 restatement firms.
No regression-level standard errors or exact p-values are printed. The tables provide t-statistics and significance markers; unknown t degrees of freedom are left unspecified.

Table 4 monthly risk-factor premiums are retained only as raw factor-input summaries for retained model variables. Cost-of-capital rows and annualized values are excluded. Its printed size-factor label is SML, while the regressions label the factor SMB; that mapping remains unclear.

The source-selected principal family is the comparison of analysts’ annual EPS forecasts against simple random-walk forecasts across FY1, FY2, and FY3 horizons. Section 2.3 describes comparing forecast accuracy; Section 3 explains that RW forecasts use lagged realized annual EPS and require no parameter estimates; Table 3 reports mean differences in absolute forecast errors by horizon and two-tailed tests. These are mean-comparison tests, not fitted regression equations, so the principal analysis has no eligible baseline regression.

The only regression identified in the relevant main-results discussion is footnote 18’s untabulated seemingly unrelated regression check relating returns to the two forecast errors at each of 36 horizons. The authors describe it as an additional test of market weighting of forecast errors, separate from the forecast-accuracy question. It is neither the principal family nor a construction regression required for a retained model. FY3 is calculated from FY2 and long-term growth, and RW is a parameter-free lagged-earnings benchmark; neither construction is an estimated regression.

estimation_procedure.description: One full-sample firm-year regression for each Table 4 panel, with a common intercept and one slope for each region-specific explanatory earnings amount. The small-loss and small-profit regions each comprise six adjacent 0.005-wide intervals below and above zero, respectively. The region labels follow the indicated earnings distribution; Table 4 uses the 0.005 bins shown in Figs. 2 and 3, which plot earnings scaled by beginning-of-year market value of common equity, while the Table 4 regression values themselves are undeflated. The table reports F-tests of bSL=bSP and bL=bP; the separate-intercept version mentioned in footnote 17 is a robustness specification, not the tabulated model.

estimation_procedure.description: One full-sample firm-year regression for each Table 4 panel, with a common intercept and one slope for each region-specific explanatory earnings amount. The small-loss and small-profit regions each comprise six adjacent 0.005-wide intervals below and above zero, respectively. The region labels follow the indicated earnings distribution; Table 4 uses the 0.005 bins shown in Figs. 2 and 3, which plot earnings scaled by beginning-of-year market value of common equity, while the Table 4 regression values themselves are undeflated. review_notes: The principal empirical claim is that asymmetric income-tax and special-item effects contribute to the earnings-distribution discontinuity. The two parallel full-sample regressions in Section 4/Table 4 directly test those channels: Eq. (1)/Panel A uses net income and region-partitioned pretax income; Eq. (2)/Panel B uses pretax income and region-partitioned income before special items. The distribution plots, effective-tax and special-item summaries, and transition tables are non-regression analyses; later deflator/measure alternatives are follow-up checks, not additional baseline regression families.

The source names no underlying estimator for the Table 4 regressions, so method remains unknown and status is needs_review. The parsed Eq. (1) source text renders its final residual symbol as “tt”; a targeted crop of physical PDF page 11 appears to show ν_t, but this symbol was not independently transcribed and equation_text is left null for Eq. (1). The complete dependent variable and RHS inventory are legible in the supplied reading text. Physical pages 11 and 12 were viewed as equation crops; no OCR was used.

models.model_label: Future returns on accrual portfolio rank, consistent-signal indicator and interaction, and controls (Equation 3; Table 4 Panel B)
models.sample_description: Full-sample firm-years from 1981–1996 with Compustat financial statement and CRSP return data and available analyst forecast revisions, subject to the paper’s nonmissing-data, firm-size, and share-price filters. The selected full-control model is estimated in separate annual regressions for return horizons t+1, t+2, and t+3. Table 4 reports the number of annual fits by horizon but not observation N for any fit; other missing controls also make analysis counts vary.
models.method_details: The authors report separate annual regressions but do not name the estimator used for the Table 4 fits; it is left unknown.

dependent_variable.name: R_{t+i}
dependent_variable.definition: Twelve-month size-adjusted buy-and-hold return, including dividends, for horizon i = 1, 2, or 3. Size adjustment subtracts the buy-and-hold return of the firm’s assigned size portfolio. The return window begins at the start of the fourth month after fiscal year-end; size portfolios are formed from NYSE/AMEX firms ranked into deciles by beginning-of-year market value of equity, and sample firms are assigned by their beginning-of-year equity value.
dependent_variable.formula: R_{t+i} = firm 12-month buy-and-hold return including dividends − buy-and-hold return of the assigned size-decile portfolio; i ∈ {1,2,3}.

evidence.quote: Future returns, Rtþi, are twelve-month size-adjusted buy-and-hold returns, inclusive of dividends.
To size-adjust a firm’s return, we subtract from the firm’s buy-and-hold return the buy-and-hold return to its size-matched portfolio.

To calculate this adjustment, we rank all sample firms that are traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and American Stock Exchange (AMEX) into 10 portfolios based on market value of equity at the beginning of the year.
We then assign each sample firm to one of the portfolios based on the firm’s market value of equity at the beginning of the year and calculate the buy-and-hold return for each size portfolio.
returns window begins at
As with all of our tests, i ranges from one to three.

independent_variables.name: C
independent_variables.definition: Year-t indicator for consistent accrual and analyst forecast-revision signals about low earnings persistence: one when Accruals_t is negative and the consensus forecast for year t+1 is revised upward around the year-t earnings announcement, or Accruals_t is positive and that forecast is revised downward; zero otherwise. Accruals uses the paper’s total-accrual measure: Accruals are [(change in current assets − change in cash and cash equivalents) − (change in current liabilities − change in debt included in current liabilities) − depreciation and amortization expense], scaled by average total assets. The paper’s general rank-scaling statement does not clarify whether this binary indicator is rank-scaled.
independent_variables.formula: C_t = 1 if Accruals_t < 0 and Revision_t > 0, or Accruals_t > 0 and Revision_t < 0; 0 otherwise. Whether C is subsequently portfolio-rank scaled is unclear.

evidence.quote: Specifically, for each of the 10 accrual portfolios we identify firms as having consistent signals when Accruals is negative (positive) and Revision is positive (negative).

An observation is included in the consistent signals subsample if the mean consensus analyst forecast for year t þ 1 is revised upward (downward) in the month of the year t earnings announcement and year t accruals are negative (positive); otherwise it is included in the inconsistent signals subsample.
C is an indicator variable that equals one for firms with accruals and analyst forecast revisions that are consistent in indicating low earnings persistence, and zero otherwise.

Accruals 1⁄4 ðDCA � DCASHÞ � ðDCL � DSTDÞ � DEP, where DCA 1⁄4 change in current assets, DCASH 1⁄4 change in cash/cash equivalents, DCL 1⁄4 change in current liabilities, DSTD 1⁄4 change in debt included in current liabilities, and DEP 1⁄4 depreciation and amortization expense, all scaled by average total assets.
All explanatory variables are scaled portfolio ranks.

research_interest_evidence.quote: C is an indicator variable that equals one for firms with accruals and analyst forecast revisions that are consistent in indicating low earnings persistence, and zero otherwise.
If consistent signals are associated with more or less accurate pricing of accruals than are inconsistent signals, d1C will differ from zero.

independent_variables.research_interest_reason: C is the consistent-signal main-effect indicator; the selected H5 prediction concerns the accrual slope and its interaction with C, while C adjusts the group intercept.

independent_variables.name: RAccruals
independent_variables.definition: Year-t rank of the accrual portfolio, scaled to the zero-to-one range. The ranked quantity is the paper’s total Accruals measure: Accruals are [(change in current assets − change in cash and cash equivalents) − (change in current liabilities − change in debt included in current liabilities) − depreciation and amortization expense], scaled by average total assets.
independent_variables.formula: RAccruals_t = year-t accrual-portfolio rank scaled to [0,1], where Accruals is Accruals_t = [(ΔCA_t − ΔCash_t) − (ΔCL_t − ΔSTD_t) − Dep_t] / average total assets_t, where ΔCA is change in current assets, ΔCash is change in cash/cash equivalents, ΔCL is change in current liabilities, ΔSTD is change in debt included in current liabilities, and Dep is depreciation and amortization expense.

evidence.quote: RAccruals equals the portfolio rank of accruals, scaled to range from zero to one.
RAccruals is the rank of the accrual portfolio in year t, scaled to be between zero and one.

Accruals 1⁄4 ðDCA � DCASHÞ � ðDCL � DSTDÞ � DEP, where DCA 1⁄4 change in current assets, DCASH 1⁄4 change in cash/cash equivalents, DCL 1⁄4 change in current liabilities, DSTD 1⁄4 change in debt included in current liabilities, and DEP 1⁄4 depreciation and amortization expense, all scaled by average total assets.

research_interest_evidence.quote: Based on Sloan (1996), we expect that d1 is negative.
If consistent signals are associated with more or less accurate pricing of accruals than are inconsistent signals, d1C will differ from zero.

independent_variables.research_interest_reason: The accrual portfolio-rank coefficient tests the predicted relation between accruals and future returns.

Significance is based on time-series standard errors of the coefficient means. The paper does not identify a within-annual-regression standard-error correction or clustering method.

estimation_procedure.description: Separate annual cross-sectional regressions are fit for each return horizon i = 1, 2, and 3. Table 4 reports 16 annual fits for t+1, 15 for t+2, and 14 for t+3 and summarizes their coefficients as time-series means and standard deviations. These are counts of fitted annual regressions, not observation N.

evidence.quote: As with all of our tests, i ranges from one to three.
There are 16, 15, and 14 annual regressions when Rtþ1, Rtþ2, and Rtþ3 is the dependent variable, respectively.
Panel B: Regression summary statistics

preprocessing.description: The source states that all explanatory variables are scaled portfolio ranks. The separate Table 4 definition of C specifies a zero/one indicator; the source does not clarify whether C or the constructed C_RAccruals term is rank-scaled after construction.

evidence.quote: All explanatory variables are scaled portfolio ranks.
C is an indicator variable that equals one for firms with accruals and analyst forecast revisions that are consistent in indicating low earnings persistence, and zero otherwise.

scope.quote: Strikingly, a combined strategy that uses forecast revisions to refine the accrual strategy generates a hedge return of 28.5%.
Our primary tests build on prior research that documents market anomalies related to accruals and revisions of analyst earnings forecasts.

To test hypothesis H5 and H5_Alt, regarding the relation between future returns and the accrual component of current earnings, we estimate the relation between the portfolio rank of accruals and future returns.

To ensure that any significant relation between current year accruals and future returns is incremental to other factors identified in prior research as predictors of future returns, we also estimate equation (3):
Table 4, panel B, presents summary statistics from estimating equations (2) and (3).

The next two columns reveal that although the relations between future returns and the control variables generally are consistent with prior research, their inclusion in equation (3) does not affect our inferences relating to RAccruals or C_RAccruals.

sample.quote: The sample comprises all firm years with available data on the Compustat annual industrial and research files and on the CRSP monthly stock returns file for NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ firms.
Our sample period is 1981 to 1996.

We eliminate firms lacking financial statement data needed to calculate accruals, e.g., financial institutions. We also impose minimum size criteria; we require firms to have sales greater than $25 million, total assets greater than $50 million, and a share price between $1 and $250.
This results in a sample of 24,343 firm-year observations with the required financial statement and returns data; analyst forecast revisions are available for 20,927 of these.
Missing data for other variables results in varying numbers of observations across analyses.

review_notes: Selected the full-control Equation (3) return-predictability family in Table 4 Panel B. The paper’s central contribution concerns how analyst forecast revisions refine the accrual pricing signal; Equation (3) is the final full-control regression of future returns on the accrual rank, consistent-signal indicator and interaction, and return predictors. Equation (2) is the reduced-control version and is excluded under the full-control rule. Equation (1) tests the antecedent forecast-revision/persistence relation; Equations (4)–(5) are later persistence analyses, outside this selected pricing family.

The body Equation (3) on physical page 9 prints δ5 for both Beta and VOL, while the Table 4 Panel B selected equation on physical page 20 prints δ5 for Beta and δ6 for VOL. The RHS terms are all identifiable; the selected model follows the full-control table equation and preserves this coefficient-label discrepancy for review.

The supplied checked transcription confirms C_RAccruals = C × RAccruals. The paper defines C as a zero/one indicator and separately says all explanatory variables are scaled portfolio ranks, but does not clarify whether the binary C or the interaction is rank-scaled.

The underlying estimator for the annual regressions is not named. Table 4 reports 16, 15, and 14 annual fits at horizons t+1, t+2, and t+3, but not an exact observation count for any fit; sample_size is therefore null.

models.model_label: Analyst-period TPRANK on lagged TPRANK performance (Table 5, Panel A)
models.sample_description: Analyst-by-semi-annual-period observations from the 2000–2009 12-month-ahead target-price sample. One within-analyst TPRANK is computed per semi-annual period, with at least three target-price forecasts required for each analyst-period. Table 5 Panel A reports 18,574 observations.
models.method_details: Table 5 reports OLS and logistic regressions; the continuous TPRANK measure is estimated with OLS.

dependent_variable.name: TPRANK
dependent_variable.definition: Within-analyst rank correlation between forecasted and realized returns for stocks covered during a semi-annual period. Forecasted return is (TP−P)/P and realized return is (P12−P)/P; P is the closing price three trading days before target-price release and P12 is the price 12 months after release. Dividends are ignored in both returns.
dependent_variable.formula: For analyst a and period s, rank-correlation across covered stocks of forecast return (TP−P)/P and realized return (P12−P)/P.

evidence.quote: First, we compute the within-analyst rank correlation (TPRANK) between forecasted and realized returns for stocks covered by an analyst in a semi-annual measurement period detailed below.

Realized return for a covered stock is calculated as (P12-P)/P, where P12 is the stock price 12-months following the target price release date, and P is the closing price three trading days before the target price release date.
An analyst’s forecasted return on a covered stock is calculated as (TP-P)/P, where TP is the target price forecast.
We ignore dividends in both realized and forecasted returns for simplicity.
For TPRANK, we calculate one rank correlation for each analyst in each semi-annual period.

independent_variables.name: LagTPPERF
independent_variables.definition: Analyst-specific ranking of prior target-price performance, based on the performance measure used for this model and target prices from the preceding measurement semi-annual period. The assigned quintile is normalized to the [0,1] range.

evidence.quote: LagTPPERF is the analyst-specific past performance ranking measured as (quintile-1)/4.
LagTPPERF measures analysts’ prior target price forecasting ability and is based on target prices released in the measurement semi-annual period.
The LagTPPERF variables are transformed to range between 0 and 1 (i.e., [Quintile-1]/4).

research_interest_evidence.quote: If analysts exhibit persistent abilities to forecast target prices, the coefficient on LagTPPERF will be positive.

The coefficients of LagTPPERF are positive and significant when |TPERROR|, TPMETEND, and TPMETANY are measures of target price forecasting ability, indicating analysts have persistent differential abilities to accurately forecast target price when controlling for other variables.

independent_variables.research_interest_reason: LagTPPERF is the primary predictor for the paper’s persistence prediction about analysts’ target-price forecasting ability.

preprocessing.description: Target-price forecasts and actual stock prices are converted to the same split-adjusted basis. The sample excludes non-12-month horizons, observations missing the pre-release or 12-month price, share prices below $1, and extreme TP/P ratios (bottom one percent or greater than four); TPRANK additionally requires at least three target-price forecasts per analyst in a semi-annual period.

evidence.quote: We use target price forecasts and actual stock prices converted to the same split-adjusted basis.
First, they must be 12-month
Less: Target prices without 12-month forecast horizon (14,603)
Second, we require the firm’s closing share price three trading days before the release date of target price forecast.
Less: Observations with stock prices less than one dollar (1,841)
Third, to determine target price performance, we require share price 12 months (252 trading days) after the target price release date.

Fourth, to mitigate the effects of extreme observations due to data errors or misaligned stock split factors, we delete observations with TP/P ratio falling into the bottom percentile of the distribution and observations with TP/P ratio greater than 4.
Finally, to estimate TPRANK, we require each analyst to issue at least three target prices in a semi-annual period.

scope.quote: We examine the overall and individual analyst accuracy of 12-month-ahead target price forecasts and assess whether analysts exhibit persistent differential abilities to forecast them.

dependent_variable.name: |TPERROR|
dependent_variable.definition: Absolute target-price forecast error. TPERROR is (P12−TP)/P, where P12 is the actual closing stock price 12 months after the target-price release and P is the closing price three trading days before release; absolute value removes the sign.
dependent_variable.formula: |TPERROR| = |(P12 − TP) / P|.

evidence.quote: Second, we compute target price forecast error (TPERROR) as (P12-TP)/P.
We report descriptive statistics for TPERROR and |TPERROR|, but we only use the latter in our tests.

Realized return for a covered stock is calculated as (P12-P)/P, where P12 is the stock price 12-months following the target price release date, and P is the closing price three trading days before the target price release date.

estimation_procedure.description: The analyst-specific LagTPPERF score is formed from target prices released in a measurement semi-annual period, ranked into quintiles and transformed to [0,1]. Current performance is measured in the subsequent test period. For the multivariate fits, the unit of analysis is an individual target-price performance observation.

evidence.quote: More specifically, we partition our 10-year sample period into 20 semi-annual periods, labeled 2000-1, 2000-2, 2001-1, etc.

To maintain independence in prices and avoid artificially inducing a positive relation between current and subsequent performance, we define test periods as the 12 months following the measurement periods.
LagTPPERF measures analysts’ prior target price forecasting ability and is based on target prices released in the measurement semi-annual period.
In our multivariate tests, the unit of analysis is individual target price performance.

preprocessing.description: Target-price forecasts and actual stock prices are converted to the same split-adjusted basis. The sample excludes non-12-month horizons, observations missing the pre-release or 12-month price, share prices below $1, and extreme TP/P ratios (bottom one percent or greater than four); TPRANK additionally requires at least three target-price forecasts per analyst in a semi-annual period.

evidence.quote: We use target price forecasts and actual stock prices converted to the same split-adjusted basis.
First, they must be 12-month
Less: Target prices without 12-month forecast horizon (14,603)
Second, we require the firm’s closing share price three trading days before the release date of target price forecast.
Less: Observations with stock prices less than one dollar (1,841)
Third, to determine target price performance, we require share price 12 months (252 trading days) after the target price release date.

Fourth, to mitigate the effects of extreme observations due to data errors or misaligned stock split factors, we delete observations with TP/P ratio falling into the bottom percentile of the distribution and observations with TP/P ratio greater than 4.
Finally, to estimate TPRANK, we require each analyst to issue at least three target prices in a semi-annual period.

scope.quote: We examine the overall and individual analyst accuracy of 12-month-ahead target price forecasts and assess whether analysts exhibit persistent differential abilities to forecast them.
Table 5 presents the results of our multivariate analyses.
Panel B reports the results of estimating Eq. (1).
TPPERF = |TPERROR|
Panel B: Regression analysis with control variables (multivariate analysis)

method.quote: We operationalize the multivariate tests using OLS (logistic) regressions when target price is measured as a continuous (an indicator) variable
This table presents OLS and logistic regressions of analysts’ current target price performance (TPPERF) on their lagged target price forecast performance (LagTPPERF) and various control variables.

sample.quote: We retain target prices issued for US firms by identifiable analysts spanning the calendar years 2000 through 2009, which meet certain criteria.
We restrict our sample to 12-month target price forecasts so the one-year period following a target price forecast release date is our forecast horizon.

Second, we require the firm’s closing share price three trading days before the release date of target price forecast.
Less: Observations with stock prices less than one dollar (1,841)
Third, to determine target price performance, we require share price 12 months (252 trading days) after the target price release date.

Fourth, to mitigate the effects of extreme observations due to data errors or misaligned stock split factors, we delete observations with TP/P ratio falling into the bottom percentile of the distribution and observations with TP/P ratio greater than 4.

estimation_procedure.description: The analyst-specific LagTPPERF score is formed from target prices released in a measurement semi-annual period, ranked into quintiles and transformed to [0,1]. Current performance is measured in the subsequent test period. For the multivariate fits, the unit of analysis is an individual target-price performance observation.

evidence.quote: More specifically, we partition our 10-year sample period into 20 semi-annual periods, labeled 2000-1, 2000-2, 2001-1, etc.

To maintain independence in prices and avoid artificially inducing a positive relation between current and subsequent performance, we define test periods as the 12 months following the measurement periods.
LagTPPERF measures analysts’ prior target price forecasting ability and is based on target prices released in the measurement semi-annual period.
In our multivariate tests, the unit of analysis is individual target price performance.

preprocessing.description: Target-price forecasts and actual stock prices are converted to the same split-adjusted basis. The sample excludes non-12-month horizons, observations missing the pre-release or 12-month price, share prices below $1, and extreme TP/P ratios (bottom one percent or greater than four); TPRANK additionally requires at least three target-price forecasts per analyst in a semi-annual period.

evidence.quote: We use target price forecasts and actual stock prices converted to the same split-adjusted basis.
First, they must be 12-month
Less: Target prices without 12-month forecast horizon (14,603)
Second, we require the firm’s closing share price three trading days before the release date of target price forecast.
Less: Observations with stock prices less than one dollar (1,841)
Third, to determine target price performance, we require share price 12 months (252 trading days) after the target price release date.

Fourth, to mitigate the effects of extreme observations due to data errors or misaligned stock split factors, we delete observations with TP/P ratio falling into the bottom percentile of the distribution and observations with TP/P ratio greater than 4.
Finally, to estimate TPRANK, we require each analyst to issue at least three target prices in a semi-annual period.

scope.quote: We examine the overall and individual analyst accuracy of 12-month-ahead target price forecasts and assess whether analysts exhibit persistent differential abilities to forecast them.
Table 5 presents the results of our multivariate analyses.
Panel B reports the results of estimating Eq. (1).
TPPERF = TPMETEND

method.quote: We operationalize the multivariate tests using OLS (logistic) regressions when target price is measured as a continuous (an indicator) variable
This table presents OLS and logistic regressions of analysts’ current target price performance (TPPERF) on their lagged target price forecast performance (LagTPPERF) and various control variables.

estimation_procedure.description: The analyst-specific LagTPPERF score is formed from target prices released in a measurement semi-annual period, ranked into quintiles and transformed to [0,1]. Current performance is measured in the subsequent test period. For the multivariate fits, the unit of analysis is an individual target-price performance observation.

evidence.quote: More specifically, we partition our 10-year sample period into 20 semi-annual periods, labeled 2000-1, 2000-2, 2001-1, etc.

To maintain independence in prices and avoid artificially inducing a positive relation between current and subsequent performance, we define test periods as the 12 months following the measurement periods.
LagTPPERF measures analysts’ prior target price forecasting ability and is based on target prices released in the measurement semi-annual period.
In our multivariate tests, the unit of analysis is individual target price performance.

preprocessing.description: Target-price forecasts and actual stock prices are converted to the same split-adjusted basis. The sample excludes non-12-month horizons, observations missing the pre-release or 12-month price, share prices below $1, and extreme TP/P ratios (bottom one percent or greater than four); TPRANK additionally requires at least three target-price forecasts per analyst in a semi-annual period.

evidence.quote: We use target price forecasts and actual stock prices converted to the same split-adjusted basis.
First, they must be 12-month
Less: Target prices without 12-month forecast horizon (14,603)
Second, we require the firm’s closing share price three trading days before the release date of target price forecast.
Less: Observations with stock prices less than one dollar (1,841)
Third, to determine target price performance, we require share price 12 months (252 trading days) after the target price release date.

Fourth, to mitigate the effects of extreme observations due to data errors or misaligned stock split factors, we delete observations with TP/P ratio falling into the bottom percentile of the distribution and observations with TP/P ratio greater than 4.
Finally, to estimate TPRANK, we require each analyst to issue at least three target prices in a semi-annual period.

scope.quote: We examine the overall and individual analyst accuracy of 12-month-ahead target price forecasts and assess whether analysts exhibit persistent differential abilities to forecast them.
Table 5 presents the results of our multivariate analyses.
Panel B reports the results of estimating Eq. (1).
TPPERF = TPMETANY

method.quote: We operationalize the multivariate tests using OLS (logistic) regressions when target price is measured as a continuous (an indicator) variable
This table presents OLS and logistic regressions of analysts’ current target price performance (TPPERF) on their lagged target price forecast performance (LagTPPERF) and various control variables.

scope.quote: We examine the relation between proximity to debt covenant violation and the following three measures of earnings management: accounting earnings management, real earnings management, and total earnings management.
Our results indicate that firms close to violation or in technical default of debt covenants engage in higher levels of TEM compared to firms far from violation.
Equation (7) is our starting point and focuses on the debt covenant incentive to manage earnings
Our study differs from Kim et al. (2011) in several aspects. First, we examine total earnings management (TEM) as well as both AEM and REM.
EM in Eq. (7) is either AEM or REM or TEM.
Table 2 Relation between proximity to covenant violation and earnings management

method.quote: We estimate the following model using quantile regression
All regression models are estimated using quantile regression

equation.quote: EM 1⁄4 a0 þ a1CLOSE þ a2DEFAULT
TEM 1⁄4 a0
Panel A: Total earnings management
TEM 1⁄4 a0 þ a1CLOSE þ a2DEFAULT þ a3PCOST þ a4DIV þ a5PERFORM þ a6DGDP þ a7MTB
a8VOL SALES þ a9VOL CASH þ a10OPER <u>LEV</u> þ a11SEO þ n

scope.quote: We examine the relation between proximity to debt covenant violation and the following three measures of earnings management: accounting earnings management, real earnings management, and total earnings management.

scope.quote: We examine the relation between proximity to debt covenant violation and the following three measures of earnings management: accounting earnings management, real earnings management, and total earnings management.

Our study differs from Kim et al. (2011) in several aspects. First, we examine total earnings management (TEM) as well as both AEM and REM.

review_notes: Scope: select Equation (7) / Table 2 Panels A–C as one principal family for the source’s central covenant-proximity question, retaining all three TEM proxies, all three AEM proxies, and all four REM outcomes. The introduction states the relation is examined across AEM, REM, and TEM; Table 2 is the first main empirical test. Later SOX, financial-distress, analyst-forecast, governance, and debt-feature analyses are separate follow-up questions and are excluded.

The modified-Jones construction has a source scaling inconsistency: Eq. (1) fits TAC_q/A_(q−1), but Eq. (2) prints TAC_q without that denominator before subtracting the fitted scaled terms. The formula is recorded as printed and the mismatch is flagged for AEMDA and downstream measures.
The source defines quantile regression for Table 2 but does not report the fitted quantile. Eqs. (4)–(6) are residual-generating fits whose estimator is not named; no OLS assumption is added.
Eq. (6) and its accompanying prose conflict over the CFO denominator. This affects REMCFO and every retained variable using REMCOMBINE. Supporting-fit sample counts are not reported.
results_review_notes: All 10 selected Table 2 baseline fits, their 117 frozen predictors, intercepts, coefficient estimates and direct p-values, fit-level Wald/LR rows, and fit observation counts are retained. Table 2 does not report coefficient standard errors or identify the fitted quantile.
Table 2 note says financial variables are winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles; this applies to the regression models. Firm and quarter-year indicators are YES, with no coefficients reported.

Table 1 descriptives are retained for 14 matched baseline outcomes and related current-ratio, market-to-book, CFO and assets measures. It reports no values for the other retained controls; non-retained leverage, ROA and debt-size rows are excluded.

Table 1 reports Mean, Q1, Median, and Q3 by CLOSE/DEFAULT/FAR group (Obs.=1,655/2,927/10,234). Those are group Ns, not variable-specific Ns, and the descriptive groups do not equal every complete-case Table 2 fit sample.
Table 2 prints ΔGDP and the clipped Panel B label REMCOMBIN; stable model-local terms are retained by named table row and column. The panel row maps to the specification variable REMCOMBINE.

The paper describes REMCOMBINE as REMPROD minus REMEXP minus REMCFO after reversing the signs of the latter components (p. 11), while Table 6 calls it the sum of the three components (p. 30). Both source statements are preserved.

review_notes: Principal family decision: Table 4 Panel B column 1 is the source-labeled baseline test of IFRS adoption on Synchronicity with full firm- and country-level controls. Columns 2–3 add the analyst-following moderator in a later conditioning analysis; columns 4–5 are country-median-adjusted sensitivity specifications, so they are not selected as the principal family.

Supporting fits retained recursively: the Eq. (1) firm-year market-model regressions generate R-squared used to construct Synchronicity, and the Eq. (3) probit generates Lambda used in the Table 4 column 1 second stage.

dependent_variable.name: Δ/MVA1
dependent_variable.definition: One-year cash-tax nonconformity Δ scaled by beginning market value of assets MVA1, with beginning book value of assets substituted when MVA is missing. Table 4 defines Δ as TXPD less the change in TXR and .35 times pre-tax income. Section 2.2 calls TXR a tax refund receivable and reports τ=34% for fiscal years ended 1998 through 1992 and 35% for 1993–2014; Table 4 instead calls TXR tax reserves and specifies .35×PI. These source discrepancies are unresolved; the formula follows the measure-specific Table 4 definition.
dependent_variable.formula: ((TXPD − (TXR_t − TXR_{t−1})) − 0.35×PI) / MVA1; MVA = BVA + (MVE − BVE); MVA1 is beginning MVA, computed as AT + ((PRCC_Q×CSHO) − SEQ), with beginning BVA substituted when MVA is missing.

evidence.quote: Δ is equal to cash taxes paid minus the change in tax reserves
(TXPD – (TXRt – TXRt-1))
less the statutory rate times pre-tax book income (.35 * PI)
Therefore, we adjust cash taxes paid by the change (δ) in a firm’s tax refund receivable (TXR).
We set τ equal to 34% for fiscal years ended 1998 through 1992 and to 35% for fiscal years ended 1993 through 2014 in our analyses.
MVA 1⁄4 BVA þ ðMVE−BVEÞ ð4Þ
where BVA is equal to a firm’s book value of assets, MVE is the firm’s market value of equity, and BVE is the firm’s book value of equity.

models.model_label: Forecast revision response by analyst ability group (80% threshold)
models.sample_description: Individual analyst forecast revision events for one-year-ahead annual earnings announced in 1990–1994. The data intersect Compustat, CRSP and I/B/E/S; events require the relevant earnings, three-day return-window, prior analyst-firm forecast-ability and forecast-surprise data. Firms must have at least five brokerage houses following them in each year 1988–1994, and each analyst-firm pair must have at least five forecasts in the preceding two years with at least one in each year. The three-day revision window must not overlap another same-firm revision, earnings announcement or dividend declaration. The final sample has 15,446 revision events.

independent_variables.name: FR_ijt × SUP_ijt
independent_variables.definition: Forecast surprise multiplied by SUP_ijt, which is one if analyst j is classified as superior for firm i at time t and zero otherwise. Forecast surprise is the analyst’s current EPS forecast less the same analyst’s most recent EPS forecast for the same firm, divided by firm i’s share price two days before the revision. At the selected 80% threshold, superior means 80% or more of that analyst’s forecasts for the firm in the preceding two years were closer to actual earnings than the contemporaneous I/B/E/S consensus. dependent_variable.formula: ACCL_t / TA_(t−1)

evidence.quote: The displayed KS equation is ACCL_t/TA_(t-1) = c0 + c1*(REV_t/TA_(t-1))*(ART_(t-1)/REV_(t-1)) + c2*(EXP_t/TA_(t-1))*(OCAL_(t-1)/EXP_(t-1)) + c3*(GPPE_t/TA_(t-1))*(DEP_(t-1)/GPPE_(t-1)) + epsilon_t.
ACCL = Net Income (#172)-Operating Cash flow (#308)
TA = Total assets (#6)
Our total accruals are calculated from statement of cash flow.

evidence.quote: The displayed KS equation is ACCL_t/TA_(t-1) = c0 + c1*(REV_t/TA_(t-1))*(ART_(t-1)/REV_(t-1)) + c2*(EXP_t/TA_(t-1))*(OCAL_(t-1)/EXP_(t-1)) + c3*(GPPE_t/TA_(t-1))*(DEP_(t-1)/GPPE_(t-1)) + epsilon_t.
REV = Revenues (#12)
ART = Accounts receivable (#2) less Tax receivables (#161)
TA = Total assets (#6)

independent_variables.name: (EXP_t / TA_(t−1)) × (OCAL_(t−1) / EXP_(t−1))

evidence.quote: The displayed KS equation is ACCL_t/TA_(t-1) = c0 + c1*(REV_t/TA_(t-1))*(ART_(t-1)/REV_(t-1)) + c2*(EXP_t/TA_(t-1))*(OCAL_(t-1)/EXP_(t-1)) + c3*(GPPE_t/TA_(t-1))*(DEP_(t-1)/GPPE_(t-1)) + epsilon_t.
EXP = expenses = Revenue (#12)- Operating income before depreciation (#13)

The Table 2 and Table 4 underlying estimators are not identified and remain null. Exact N per year-by-industry KS construction fit is unreported; 10 is a minimum cell size.
results_review_notes: The retained baseline family consists of the two large-sample Table 2 regressions and the two restatement-sample Table 4 regressions; later rank regressions, market-to-book robustness, the KS construction regression, and correlation panels are excluded.
All eight baseline predictor appearances are focal to Hypotheses 1 and 2: ROA and LG are the predicted relationships for EM/EM_Restated and EQ/EQ_Restated.

Individual coefficient P-values are reported, but no test type, reference distribution, sidedness, degrees of freedom, standard errors, or test statistics are reported for these four result sets. None were inferred.
The estimator is not identified by the source; the word regression is not treated as evidence of OLS.
